thread:
maria: INCIDENT: noticed after a small canary shift (10%) to rw-cascade-v5 — p99 jumped from ~4.2s to ~18.9s, p95 from ~1.1s to ~3.3s. Streaming stalls increasing on chunked responses. Paging oncall.
incident-bot: :rotating_light: SEV-2: High latency detected (hosted-api-us-east). Alert rule: service_response_latency_p99 > 10s for 3m. Pager: @ajay
ajay: I'm up. pulling graphs now. which route saw the traffic change?
maria: hosted-api /generate and /chat streaming route. Canary config: 10% -> rw-cascade-v5-quant. Canary started ~5m ago.
ajay: ok looking at traces — lots of tail latency on seqs > 1024 tokens. KV cache miss pattern looks different vs v4. Could be kernel selection regressions with new compile path.
leo: I see streaming stalls in the logs: repeated `timeout waiting for chunk` on connection pool for a subset of workers. p99 for chunk latency ~12s.
olivia: adding customer impact: two enterprise tenants in us-east saw elevated error budgets; support ticket #2026-84 opened by AcmeCorp. Sales-ops pinged.
sales-ops: Thanks — we got the ticket. Sales aware, will stand by.
ajay: immediate mitigation options: 1) scale down canary to 0% 2) route canary to slower but stable pool 3) force rollback to rw-cascade-v4. Which is fastest?
maria: option 1 or 3 preferred. 0% traffic split is quickest and reversible if things look stable.
kim: I can set traffic back to 0% now. running command.
kim: ```
# set canary weight to 0
redwoodctl rollout update --route hosted-api-us-east --model rw-cascade-v5-quant --weight 0
``` 
kim: submitted, API returned 202. Applying traffic change across hosts.
ajay: watching p99 — pulling prometheus: 
```promql
histogram_quantile(0.99, sum(rate(http_request_duration_seconds_bucket{route="/chat"}[2m])) by (le))
```
ajay: p99 dropping — was 18.9s, now 5.1s and trending down. streaming stalls count decreasing.
maria: good. keep an eye for residual errors. we should decide whether to rollback the canary or re-run compilation with fallback kernels.
dave: collecting logs from the canary hosts; attaching short stack traces. looks like a memory growth in kernel selection path on sequence lengths > 1024.
leo: I recommend rollback for now and open a follow-up for engine/regression. rollback command:
```
redwoodctl rollout set --route hosted-api-us-east --model rw-cascade-v4 --percent 100
```
kim: initiating rollback to v4 at 1768865700.
incident-bot: Action logged: rollback started by kim at 1768865700.
kim: rollback completed, route now on rw-cascade-v4 @100%.
ajay: re-evaluating metrics — p99 now ~1.2s, p95 ~0.9s. streaming stalls resolved for the top customers. error rate normalized.
maria: customer impact: AcmeCorp saw degraded quality for ~6m (10:12–10:18 UTC); support ticket updated. not seeing broader SLA breaches but we did touch error budgets for two customers.
olivia: note for postmortem: mention kernel selection path, canary test workload lacked >1024 token traces and didn't trigger the regression. add synthetic long-seq tests to canary suite.
dave: I'll open a JIRA: INF-3721 with logs and stack traces.
leo: engineering action items: 1) disable v5 canary until regression fixed 2) add long-seq synthetic to canary harness 3) add a runbook step for immediate 0% split + rollback
maria: handing incident to kim for postmortem and follow-ups. kim — please coordinate with engine and QA and assign owners.
kim: ack — will own postmortem and follow-ups. tagging @ajay @dave for investigation. prepping timeline and will send first draft in ~90m.
ajay: also recommend adding a short-latency SLO alert for streaming chunk latency to catch stalls earlier.
maria: thanks everyone. closing the live mitigation. will not mark incident resolved until postmortem published.
incident-bot: Incident status: mitigation complete. Oncall handoff: kim taking ownership for next steps. Severity: SEV-2 -> Monitoring.
summary: Canary traffic shift to rw-cascade-v5 caused p99 latency spikes and streaming stalls; immediate mitigation by setting canary weight to 0% and full rollback to v4. Oncall handoff and postmortem assigned.
